title: fix(motion): turning rides keep no sample closer than half the chord share
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`: a new private step `thin` runs after the bisection in `profile_offset` and `profile_offset_in`.
- `thin` drops each sample that is closer than half the chord share (`MIN_GAP_SHARE = 0.5`) to the last kept sample.
- The first and the last sample (the window ends) always stay. At the end, a kept sample that is too near the last sample gives way to it.
- Each kept sample is an exact point of the offset curve. No new point is made.
- A chord moves by at most two gaps (one share). The callers pass a quarter of the user tolerance as the share, so the ride stays within half of the user tolerance.
- The module doc now states this bound.

## Cause

The bisection (`settle`) halves the interval toward a vertical tangent of the offset curve. The samples come closer than 1 micrometre. Exact float twins of candidate stations also occur (a gap of 1e-16 mm). `out.dedup()` removes only exactly equal samples. The lathe posts wrote these runs as identical `G01` blocks.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_spacing.rs`:

- `od_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped bar and the collar, tol 1e-2, 2.5e-3 and 1e-4.
- `id_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped hole wall.
- `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap`: the window ends 1e-7 past a candidate station. This pins the give-way at the end.
- `thinning_keeps_the_window_ends_and_the_nose`: the ends stay, and each sample is at distance d from the profile.
- `thinned_chords_stay_within_the_bound`: 9 points on each chord stand at least `d - 2 * tol` from the profile.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged `offset.rs` the OD and ID spacing pins fail with `gap 0.00000000000000044` (OD) and `gap 0.00000000000000011` (ID).

Mutations:

- The old `offset.rs`: 2 pins red. Restored: green.
- The tail give-way disabled (`while ... && false`): `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap` red (`gap 0.0000001`). Restored: green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion lib, turning_bore, turning_offset_spacing, turning_prof).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Also green by hand: motion `turning_contour`, `turning_contour_stock`. App debug: 25 lathe and turning binaries (`lathe_post*`, `turning*`, `sim_lathe_body`, `coarse_laws`, `project_roundtrip` and others).
- Release `--ignored` on 16 app lathe and turning binaries: green (1 heavy test in that set).

## Goldens moved

4 files. Each diff only removes lines (516 removed, 0 added):

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_mm.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_inch.nc` (-129)

Most removed lines are runs of identical blocks, for example 40 x `G01 X7. Z2. F0.04` and 39 x `G01 X9.1 Z3.05 F0.05`. The other removed lines are sub-gap steps at the start of the same face, for example `Z2.001` to `Z2.005`. The goldens were made again with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Not exercised

- The full heavy reach (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base main`, 223 app lanes) did not run. The author must run it on the final head before the PR is flagged ready.
- The cone-thread example of #2394 is not on main. It was not posted again.
- At a very small user tolerance (for example 0.001 mm) the gap is less than the posted resolution. Two rounded blocks can then still be equal. This costs no position.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `offset.rs` or the new test file.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2882-ride-min-spacing.md`. The post-side alternative (drop a repeated block in each lathe post) was dropped.

Written by an Opus lead + Haiku workers (lane trial). The workers wrote about 85% of the lines: `thin` and its call sites, the first four pins, and the decision record. The lead wrote about 15%: the chord-bound correction (1.5x to 2x share, because the give-way at the end can double the gap), the tail pin, the clippy fix, the golden refresh and the review.

Effort: high

Changelog: Turning profile rides no longer post runs of identical G01 blocks: samples closer than half the chord share are dropped.

Fixes #2882

title: fix(2d): refuse a no-pick chamfer on a partly bevelled edge loop by name
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer with no picks now refuses at generation when a top edge loop carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length.
The message names a point on the bevelled part and a point on the sharp part. It asks the user to pick the edges.

Example text, from the unit test fixture: `the edge loop near X1.000 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length - it is sharp near X30.500 Y0.000 - a chamfer with no picks would cut the sharp part; pick the edges to break`.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`: the new function `partly_bevelled`, and one call in `ride_loops`.
- `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs`: the plate of the issue, with and without the extra vertex.
- `docs/decisions/2887-chamfer-partly-bevelled.md`: the decision record.

The issue permits two results: a ride of the bevelled segments only, or a named refusal that asks for picks. This PR takes the refusal.

## Cause

`ride_loops` classified each top loop whole, by the farthest vertex from the wall loop.
A loop that is bevelled on one side has two readings.
With an extra vertex on the top edge of the bevel, the loop read as bevelled. The ride then cut the three sharp sides.
Without that vertex, the two bevel corners lie on the wall, and the loop read as sharp. The tip then stood inside the part at the bevel.
The verifier refused the two programs as a gouge at a coordinate, with no reason.

## The check

The check runs for each segment of the matched top loop. It measures the two ends and the middle against the wall loop.

- A segment within 1e-6 mm of the wall is sharp.
- A segment more than 0.05 mm from the wall is bevelled.
- A segment between the two values counts as neither.

The loop is refused when it has a bevelled segment and more than one chamfer width of sharp length.
The result does not depend on tessellation.

## Tests

Pins:

- `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_a_plate_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name` (app, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`)
- `the_refusal_does_not_depend_on_an_extra_vertex_on_the_bevel` (app, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name` (motion lib)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_with_an_extra_vertex_too` (motion lib)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_all_round_is_not_partly_bevelled` (motion lib)

Mutation: with `chamfer_ride.rs` of `upstream/main` 17b1b2b81, the two app pins fail (`a partly bevelled edge loop with no picks is refused: ()`: generation succeeds). With the fix, the two pins pass.
The motion unit pins were not run against the old file: they call the new function, so the old file does not compile with them.

Unchanged and green: the six older `chamfer_ride` unit tests and the seven tests of `chamfer_modelled_edge` (#303, #2435, #2596).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 7991bc04b (4 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes did not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` lists 223 steps for this diff, because a change in `motion` reaches each `app` heavy lane. They must run before this PR is flagged ready.
- A partial ride of only the bevelled segments is not in this PR. The decision record gives the reasons.
- No note lists whole loops that a no-pick chamfer leaves sharp (the #2596 case). `ride_loops` has no warning channel. That is separate work.
- Curved partly bevelled loops (a fillet on a part of an arc) have no test. The check uses three samples for each segment.
- The verifier is not changed.

## Overlaps

`chamfer_ride.rs`: no open PR changes it.
#2831 adds a field to `OpParams::Face` in each test file that builds it. The new test file here builds `OpParams::Face` too. The PR that merges second adds the field in `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs`.

Written by an Opus lead + Haiku workers (lane trial)

- Worker 1 (Haiku) wrote the guard and its unit tests, and its tests passed. The lead then lost that edit by accident during the mutation check: the copy to a save file was refused and the revert of the file ran. The lead wrote the guard again from the worker's reported diff, with small changes (`hypot`, an iterator loop, a shared fixture for the unit tests). So the lead wrote the 93 lines of `chamfer_ride.rs` that are in this PR, to the design that the lead gave the worker.
- Worker 2 (Haiku) wrote `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs` (145 lines) from the lead's mesh specification. The lead did not change it.

- In lines: workers 171 of 264 (65 %), lead 93 of 264 (35 %). The root cause, the design and the review are the lead's.

title: feat(drilling): fine boring cycle (G76) with a required shift
body:
Stacked on #2823 (merge #2823 first).

## What changed

Fine boring is a new cycle on the drilling operation. This is the last slice of #1445, and it is the work of #1479.

- `CycleChoice::FineBore { shift_x_um, shift_y_um }` is a new cycle choice. The shift is a required part of the choice. There is no default shift.
- `CycleKind::FineBore` is a new CL cycle kind. The `.cl` text writes `FineBore`. The `.cnc` stream writes `CYCLE FINEBORE`.
- The chain of one hole is: feed in, shift at the bottom, rapid out at the shifted XY, shift back at R.
- The post engine reads the shift from the chain. It gives the shift to the script as `ShiftX` and `ShiftY`.
- The post engine refuses the cycle by name for a script that does not declare `fineBoring = true`.
- The Haas post declares `fineBoring`. It writes `G76 X Y Z R I J P F`, one whole block for each hole. It never writes `Q`.
- Each of the other 17 shipped posts refuses the cycle by name.
- A machine file can state `spindle.orientation`. The value `false` refuses a fine bore with any post.
- The generator refuses a shift that the bar has no room for. The room is `(tool dia. - shank dia.) / 2`.
- The commands refuse a zero shift, a shift above 5 mm on one axis, and a shift that is not smaller than a hole radius.
- The verifier reads the three stopped-spindle rapids with the stopped bar. It still reads the shank and the holder at the shifted position.
- The reach law holds a fine bore to the shank fit in the hole, as it does for a bore and a ream.
- The project file, MCP `edit_operation` and the Cycle combo of the drill page carry the choice and its shift.

A program that does not choose the cycle posts the same bytes as before.

## Cause

Hole making had no fine boring cycle. A bore cycle rapids out with the tip on the wall, and the tip marks the finished bore.

## Design

- The shift is in the chain, not in a new record field. The posted `I` and `J` are the shift of the chain, so the two cannot disagree. The WCS flip, the WCS yaw and the axis mirror already transform the moves and the cycle centre together.
- The refusal for a post is in the engine. A new post is refused until it declares the flag.
- Haas `G76` reads `I` and `J` as the shift along X and Y. The `Q` form takes its direction from Setting 27. A program cannot state that setting, so the post never writes `Q`.
- Fanuc, Mazak and Doosan take the direction of `Q` from a control parameter. These posts refuse. #2886 has the work for these controls, for Heidenhain `CYCL DEF 202`, for Sinumerik `CYCLE86` and for Mach4.
- The verifier models the tool as the cylinder that the turning edge sweeps. That cylinder, shifted by `s`, enters the bore wall by `s`. With the spindle stopped, the bar reaches `bar radius + s` from the hole axis and the tip reaches `tool radius - s`. The two stay inside the cylinder that the feed in cut while `s < tool radius - bar radius`. The feed in was read over the same cylinder.
- The shank and the holder are not inside that cylinder. The solid law reads them at the shifted position.
- `docs/decisions/1445-fine-boring.md` has the options that were dropped.

MCP: `edit_operation` takes `"cycle": {"fine_bore": {"shift_x": 0.3, "shift_y": -0.4}}` (millimetres). The word `"fine_bore"` with no shift is refused.

## Tests

Pins:

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `drilling::tests_fine_bore` (6 tests): the chain, the choice with no default, the room door, the bore door.
- `camcraft-post`, `fine_bore_cycle` (8 tests): the stream word, the Haas `G76` block, the `P0` word, the refusal with no shift, the refusal of each other post, the machine gate, the file word, the golden.
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::fine_bore` (4 tests): the acquittal, the cases that keep each conviction, the holder that is still read.
- `camcraft-app`, `fine_bore_cycle` (9 tests): the command with undo and redo, the project file, the `.cl` text, the stamp, the command doors, the generator door, the shank fit, the Haas post, the machine gate, the post refusal, MCP.
- `camcraft-ui` lib, `egui_app::tests::cycle_combo` (3 tests) and `egui_app::tests::holes_fine_bore` (2 tests).

Red before the change: the pins do not compile on the base. `CycleChoice::fine_bore`, `CycleKind::FineBore` and `fine_bore_gate` do not exist there. This is a new cycle, so there is no old behaviour to show red at run time. The first run of the app pin on the new generator, before the verifier change, was red:

```text
the verifier accepts the shifted retract: [RapidInStock { at: 2 }, RapidInStock { at: 3 }]
post blocked - 2 warning(s): FineBore1: rapid move 2 travels through stock ...; FineBore1: rapid move 3 travels through stock ...
```

Mutations. Each one was red with the guard removed and green after the restore:

| Guard removed | Pin that went red |
|---|---|
| motion: the room door (`s >= room`) | `a_shift_the_bar_has_no_room_for_is_refused_by_name` |
| motion: the zero shift at the choice | `the_fine_bore_choice_has_no_default_shift` |
| motion: the zero shift at the generator | `a_hand_made_zero_shift_is_refused_by_the_generator` |

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |
| `params`: the allowance in the stamp | same | red |
| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |

| motion: no stock refused (`Guards::stock`) | same | red |

| motion: the film of the reading (one cell diagonal put back) | same | red |

The three motion guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior_adaptive::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off.
The first run of the two stamp mutants and of the bad-value mutant stayed green on the app tests, because another path gave the same result. I added the two lib pins for them, and the mutants are red on those pins.

## Not exercised

- The rows of the group on the 2D Adaptive page. The page keeps the value of the draft and shows no rows. Follow-up: #2884.
- The MCP skill row. The session could not write `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. Follow-up, with the row text: #2885.
- A golden CL file for the rest pass of the 2D Adaptive. The tests read the path against a simulation.
- A setup whose stock is carried from an earlier setup, a WCS yaw, and the field stock engine. The code path is that of #2822, which has the same limits.

## Known limits (recorded in `docs/decisions/1446-rest-adaptive-op.md`)

- The `entry` field and the links of the operation are not read with the group on. Each entry is a plunge into proved-clear space.

## Literature

- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", LNCS 500, Springer, 1991.
- Z. Yao, S. K. Gupta, D. S. Nau, "Algorithms for selecting cutters in multi-part milling problems", Computer-Aided Design 35(9), 2003.

These sources describe pocket geometry and cutter coverage. The stock-proof rules are the decision of this project. No code or text of a different CAM product was read or used.

title: fix(turning): allow threading passes to start in front of the end face
body:
## What changed

- Removed the post-filter push of `w0` and `w1` in `revolve::lattice` (`crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`). Every in-domain band endpoint is already in `lat`. Removing those four lines keeps `lat` strictly inside `[d_lo, d_hi]`. Free air past an end face no longer creates intervals where the scan reads `E(s) = 0` as rest.
- Computed `k_hi` in `thread_planned_in` (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`) from the unclamped `f.station_of(p.top_z)`. Kept `s_lo..=s_hi` clamped to `[d_lo, d_hi]` for `ref_top`, valley phase discovery, and the empty-window refusal. A threading pass can now start in free air in front of the end face.
- Added `crates/motion/tests/turning_thread_end_face.rs` with four pinning tests.
- Added `docs/decisions/2879-thread-free-air-start.md`.

## Cause

Two defects prevented a free-end thread from starting in front of the end face:

1. `revolve::lattice` filtered `lat` to `[d_lo, d_hi]` and then pushed `w0` and `w1` back into `lat`. Whenever a move band extended past `d_hi` (by 0.1 mm on a free-end groove, or by whole pitches on a free-air lead-in), `revolve::scan` evaluated an air interval where `E(s) = 0` and reported the capped wave floor (5.0 mm) as rest.
2. `blade::setup` clamped `s_hi` to `d_hi`, and `thread_planned_in` used that clamped `s_hi` in `k_hi`. Setting `top_z` in front of the end face (such as Z81 for a Z78 end face) still started each pass inside the bar at Z77.5.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/turning_thread_end_face.rs`:

- `free_end_groove_band_past_end_face_is_not_rest`: red before fix (`rest_mm: 5.000000000000001`), green after fix.
- `free_air_lead_in_starts_in_front_of_end_face_and_judges_clean`: red before fix (started at `77.5` instead of `80.5`), green after fix.
- `free_air_start_still_convicts_real_gouge_and_real_rest_on_part`: checks overcut, shallow cut, missed turn, and a free-air lattice point whose flank clips a solid end face.
- `groove_at_free_end_face_spilling_into_end_air_is_not_rest`: red before fix (`rest_mm: 4.0`), green after fix.

Mutation checks on `turning_thread_end_face`:

- Reverted `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (3 of 4 failed with `rest_mm: 5.0` and `rest_mm: 4.0`). Restored: green.
- Reverted `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (`free_air_lead_in_starts_in_front_of_end_face_and_judges_clean` failed: `got 77.5`). Restored: green.

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

- No UI test or physical machine run.

This PR adds the example catalog case `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread`.
The case is a spun turning profile: a cone with a threaded end.

- The part has a collar, a 20 mm to 10 mm cone over 40 mm, an 8 mm neck and an M10x1.5 thread, 15 mm long.
- The machine is the built-in `Lathe` (`assets/machines/lathe.mch`). The post is `Fanuc Lathe`.
- The program has six operations: `Face`, `Rough profile`, `Finish profile`, `Neck`, `Thread`, `Part off`.

- `README.md`, which walks through the steps

The PR also adds one test to `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` and the decision file `docs/decisions/2394-cone-thread.md`.
No file in `crates/*/src` changes.

## Cause

Issue #2394 asks for this case. The catalog infrastructure of #2393 is on `main` since v0.24.0.

## Decisions that differ from the issue text

The decision file gives each one with its reason.

- The case imports two models: the turned blank and the finished part. Profile Finish cannot finish the model that the Threading operation needs (#2880).
- The neck needs a sixth operation, a Groove Finish. The issue lists five.
- The thread posts as G32 passes, not as the G76 cycle. A G76 cycle would start inside the part (#2878, #2879).
- The threading insert is a tool definition in the script. No catalog insert fits a 1.5 mm pitch (#893).
- The shoulder has no fillet (#2881).

## Bugs filed on the way

The issue says: "Any refusal or wrong output found on the way is filed as its own bug and linked here."

- #2878 (`P1`): a G76 cycle starts inside the part.
- #2879 (`P3`): a threading pass cannot start in front of the end face.
- #2880 (`P3`): Profile Finish reads thread valleys and a neck step as rest.
- #2881 (`P3`): a steep fillet chord sends the profile ride far out of the bar.

The first form of the taper assert let the taper mutation pass. The assert now checks each block on the cone.

title: fix(multiaxis): rotary operations read a face selection or refuse it
body:
## What changed

- Rotary Parallel keeps its cut over the picked faces. The kernel plans the raster on the full model, as before. Then it keeps each cut point where the line from the axis through the ball centre meets a picked facet. The radial relink builds the links between the kept pieces.
- The axis fit, the gouge laws and the verify still read the full model.
- Rotary Parallel refuses, by name, a selection that it cannot use:
  - a pick that is not a face;
  - picks on two models;
  - a face that does not look away from the axis (an end face, a bore wall);
  - picks that form separate groups;
  - picks that no pass lies over.
- Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset refuse a face selection by name. They do not cut the full model silently. Face containment for these two kinds is not in this PR: #2851 (Rotary Contour) and #2852 (Rotary Offset) hold that work.
- The generation stamp of a rotary operation with a selection gets a version mark. A path that was cached under the old reading becomes stale.
- An operation with no selection (source `Entity` or `Stock`) generates as before.

New files:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_pick.rs`: the clip, `faces_outward`, `groups`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rotary_picks.rs`: the picks read from the world, and the refusals.
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_face_selection.rs`: the pins.
- `docs/decisions/2848-rotary-face-selection.md`: the decision record.

## Cause

`material_of` reads a selection as the full facets of the picked models. The rotary arms of `run_job` gave those facets to the kernels. No code read which faces were picked, and no code refused the selection.

## Scope against the issue's "Done means"

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| Rotary Parallel accepts `SrcRef::Selection` | done |
| Rotary Contour, Rotary Offset accept `SrcRef::Selection` | not done: they refuse by name; #2851, #2852 |
| Toolpath stays in the picked faces | done for Rotary Parallel |
| Axis fit uses the full model | done, pinned |
| Stock simulation reads only the generated toolpath | no change necessary: the simulation reads the stored path |
| UI enables face selection for rotary operations | no change necessary: `SetOperationGeometry` has one door for all kinds (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`) |
| Unusable selections refuse with a clear message | done for all three kinds |
| Full-model operation is the same | done: the `None` path is the old code |
| Tests | done |

The maintainer's triage comment names the defect: the operation ignores the selection without a message. This PR removes that for all three kinds. If the maintainer wants the issue open until #2851 and #2852 merge, change `Fixes` to `Refs`.

## Tests

Pins (`crates/app/tests/rotary_face_selection.rs`), all red on `upstream/main` 326c938b1:

- `rotary_parallel_keeps_its_cut_over_the_picked_faces` - red before: "a cut at station -16 is off the picked neck (2..16)".

- `rotary_parallel_reads_a_welded_wall_pick_as_its_strips` - red before: "a cut at station -16.204 is off the picked patch".
- `rotary_parallel_refuses_a_selection_it_cannot_use_by_name` - red before: "the selection must be refused, not cut".
- `rotary_contour_and_offset_refuse_a_face_selection_by_name` - red before: "the selection must be refused, not cut".

Unit tests (`multiaxis::rotary_pick::tests`): the clip, `faces_outward`, `groups`.

Mutations (each was put in, the pins ran, the fix was put back):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| The two rotary arms of `generate.rs` as before the fix | 5 of 5 pins red |
| The kernel clip off (`rotary_parallel_over` ignores the picks) | 3 keep pins red |
| A chain pick read as "no facets" (no "is not a face" refusal) | refusal pin red |
| The `faces_outward` guard off | refusal pin red |
| The `groups` guard off | refusal pin red |

A file-level restore of `generate.rs` from `upstream/main` does not compile with the new job field. The arm-level mutation replaced it.

title: fix(motion): the corner check reads a cusp loop that crosses itself
body:
## What changed

- `connected_pieces` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` reads each outer loop with `Region::from_slices`. Before, it used `Region::new`.
- A loop that crosses itself is now read as its even-odd lobes. The check does not stop.
- The noise filters of the check are the same (`PIECE_AREA_MIN`, `SLIVER_HALF_WIDTH`, `CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`).
- `docs/decisions/2849-corner-cusp-loop.md` records the decision.

This PR is partial work for #2849. It fixes the defect that the issue names ("loop crosses itself" in the corner check). It does not change the three toolpath tests of the issue.

## Cause

- `unreached_corners` computes `leftover = piece.difference(&swept)`. Then it calls `connected_pieces(&leftover)`.
- A bore drawn as chords leaves a cusp a few microns wide at each chord vertex.
- On the micron lattice, the boolean can return such a cusp as one loop that crosses itself.
- `Region::new` refuses that loop. The error stopped the whole corner check.
- The user then saw only the note "the check for corners of the stock tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself)".
- The defect does not need the solidcore importer. It is on `main` for a synthetic bore.

## Tests

Pin: `machining2d::unreached::law::a_chord_cusp_that_crosses_itself_does_not_stop_the_corner_check` (`camcraft-motion`, lib).

- The pin builds a 25 mm bore with 50, 60 and 63 chords. The reach is 2, 3 and 4 mm.
- It asserts that the check runs, names no corner and gives no note.
- On unchanged `upstream/main` (`326c938b1`) the pin fails: `50 chords, reach 2: invalid geometry: loop crosses itself`.
- Mutation: with `Region::new` put back, the pin is red. With `Region::from_slices`, the pin is green.

A probe sweep (not committed) used 24 to 400 chords, 9 reach values and 4 phases.

- Before the fix, 4726 of 13572 cases stopped with the error.
- After the fix, no case stops.
- After the fix, 36 cases name corners. Each has 24 to 28 chords and a reach of 8 or 10 mm. Their chord corners are larger than `CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on the final code.

- `motion lib`: ok.
- `app:adaptive_zero_margin_island`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main` shows one source file and one decision file.

## Not exercised

- The three tests of the issue with the solidcore mesh. PR B of #917 is not pushed, so the mesh is not available. The owner's diagnosis on the issue says that this fix does not change them.
- `Milling-test.step` through the solidcore reader. The pin uses a synthetic bore, not the real outline.
- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`). They did not run. They must run before this PR is flagged ready.
- A note that changes for a real project. A pocket that showed "did not run" can now show a corner note, or no note.

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs`.

PR B of #917 marks the three tests with `known-fail #2849`. This PR does not close the issue, so those markers stay valid.

Changelog: The 2D pocket corner check no longer stops with "loop crosses itself" on a bore whose outline has fine chords.

title: fix(geometry): order sheet cuts before material release
body:
Stacked on #2808 (merge #2808 first)

## What changed

Add `camcraft_geometry::nesting::cut_order` for one placed sheet.
Build a global containment forest for closed loops and open chains.
Resolve closed `Auto` sides by depth parity and open `Auto` sides to `OnLine`.
Traverse the forest iteratively. Sort siblings by enclosed area, then stable ID.
Schedule marking, internal, rough profile, and final breakthrough phases.
Use an explicit `release_phase` to distinguish blind pockets from through cuts.
Refuse invalid geometry, side requests, incomplete schedules, and cuts after material release.
Report circular-tool corner limits without changing the picked geometry.

## Cause

The geometry crate lacked one cut order across a nested sheet.
An enclosing hole can free a smaller part before that part's cuts finish.
Independent operation orders cannot enforce that sheet relationship.

## Tests

The initial pinning build failed on unchanged upstream base `f3b0e1955` with `E0432` because the planner API was absent.

title: perf(sim): share unchanged cut bricks between playback keyframes
body:
## What changed

- The three cut layers of `SdfField` (`cuts`, `cut_ups`, `cut_downs`) hold each brick in an `Arc` (`CutLayer`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field.rs`).
- A clone of the field copies the keys and the pointers only. It shares the bricks.
- A write goes through `layer_brick_mut` (`Arc::make_mut`). It copies a brick first when a clone still holds that brick.
- `claim_record` and `up_record` read the cell first. They take the writable brick only when the value changes. A move that changes no cell copies no brick.
- `KeyCost` has a new method, `key_bytes_after(prev)`. The keyframe store counts a keyframe by the bricks that the keyframe before it does not share, and by its map entries.
- `Keyframes::offer` and `Keyframes::held_bytes` use that count. The budget, the thinning and the stride law do not change.
- The public API of the sim crate only grows: `SdfField::cut_bytes_after` and `KeyCost::key_bytes_after` (with a default).

## Cause

A playback keyframe was a whole copy of the cut layers (#2181, PR #2192). Two keyframes one stride apart differ only in the bricks that the moves between them changed. The store paid for all bricks in each keyframe.

## Readings

Dense 100 mm face (`precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`, release, 4268 moves, 68 keyframes, stride 64):

| | Keyframe bytes | Calculation time |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream/main` (old sim sources) | 444 940 288 (424 MiB) | 49.8 s |
| This PR | 65 181 664 (62 MiB) | 30 s to 32 s (three runs) |

The factor is 6.8. The test asserts a factor of 6 at least.
The machine had other builds in progress, so the times are not exact.

Staged 24 mm face at 0.5 mm cells (debug, 28 keyframes): 9 923 808 bytes held. Whole copies cost 45 301 760 bytes. The factor is 4.56. The test asserts a factor of 4 at least.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` (`crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs`). It asserts the factor of 4, the equality of the running count and the audit, and the bit-identical replay at six positions.
- `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts the count on plain values, before and after a thinning.
- `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts that a clone is not written through, and that the cut over shared bricks is the plain cut, bit for bit.
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` (heavy lane, release). It now asserts the factor of 6 on the dense face.

Red before the fix: the first pin failed on unchanged code with `8454144 bytes held; whole copies cost 8454144`.

Mutations (each one red, then green after the restore):

- `offer` counts `value.key_bytes()` (the old line): `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` is red.
- `held_bytes` sums whole copies (the old line): the same test is red, `(5, 1, 40, 100)` against `(5, 1, 40, 40)`.
- `layer_brick_mut` writes through the shared pointer: `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` is red at "a shared brick is copied before the write".
- `claim_record` takes the writable slot before the read: `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` is red, `16358624 bytes held; whole copies cost 45301760`.
- All of `crates/sim/src` from `upstream/main`: `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` is red, `444940288 bytes held; whole copies cost 444940288`.

Unchanged and green: `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position`, `a_live_seek_after_a_cancel_keeps_the_byte_budget`, `the_worker_calculates_first_then_replays_and_the_post_gate_is_unchanged` (the replay is bit-identical, the budget holds, the post gate reads the same).

Gate on the final head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 11 steps, 0 failed (sim lib, `play_keys`, `play_precalc`, `stock_carry_side_exact`, `stock_columns`, `stock_field_cost`, `stock_sdf`; app `stock_field_cost`, `stock_play_precalc`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Heavy lanes that ran (release, `--ignored`): app `stock_play_precalc` and app `stock_field_cost`. The two are green.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` plans 217 steps for this diff. Only the two heavy binaries above ran. The other heavy lanes did not run. Run them before this PR is flagged ready.
- The `camcraft-ui` crate was not built. This PR changes no item that the UI crate can see, other than the two additions.
- The gate and the tests ran without sccache and with a target directory outside the worktree. The sccache daemon on this machine executed no compile, and a stuck `cargo check` of the editor tooling held the build lock of the worktree.
- `CostLedger` (the cut region, the full-brick ledger, the dirty set) is still copied whole by each keyframe. The store does not count it, as before.
- The time of one cell write was not measured alone. The dense face calculation as a whole is faster.

## Overlaps

PR #2714 changes other files in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/` and `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`. It changes none of the files of this PR.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2194-share-keyframe-bricks.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Simulation playback: keyframes share the stock bricks that no move changed, so the calculation before playback uses much less memory (the dense 100 mm face: 62 MiB, before 424 MiB) and keeps a shorter stride on large programs.

Fixes #2194

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

Pins in `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (6 tests):

title: fix(drilling): Back bore (G89) carries the dwell and feeds out at the plunge feed
body:
## What changed

- The drill generator now writes the user's dwell into the `Cycle` record of a Back bore (G89) hole.
- The Back bore chain now feeds out at the plunge feed. This is the same feed as the feed in.
- The Sinumerik post writes `P0` for a G89 hole with zero dwell. This clears a previous positive dwell.
- No golden file changed.

Files:

- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`: the two changes above.
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/tests_backbore.rs`: the two pinning tests (new file).
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/mod.rs`: registers the test module.
- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps`: writes an explicit G89 P word, including zero.
- `crates/post/tests/sinumerik_g89_dwell.rs`: pins the G89 dwell unit and the transition to zero.
- `docs/decisions/1480-backbore-dwell.md`: the decision entry.

## Cause

`drill()` set the dwell of a Back bore hole to 0. The dwell of the user did not reach the cycle record, the simulation or a post.

`drill()` also fed out at the cutting feed. A canned G89 has one F word, and the post takes it from the first cutting move of the hole, which is the plunge. The control fed out at the plunge feed, but the CL chain said the cutting feed. The verifier and the simulation read a different motion than the machine ran.

## Dwell unit for each post

The posts read the dwell in seconds and write their own P unit. The Sinumerik post now writes G89 P at zero too. These tests pin the words:

- Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan: `G89 ... P500` (whole milliseconds). `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs`.
- grblHAL, Tormach, LinuxCNC: `G89 ... P0.5` (seconds). The same file.
- Haas: `G89 ... P500`. `crates/post/tests/haas_dwell_cycles.rs`.
- Mach4: `G89 ... P0.25` (seconds). `crates/post/tests/mach4_post.rs`.
- Sinumerik: `G89 ... P500`, then `G89 ... P0`. `crates/post/tests/sinumerik_g89_dwell.rs`.
  Unit source: [Siemens ISO dialects Function Manual, 07/2021](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/254/109801254/att_1077768/v1/ONE_840Dsl_828D_iso_dialects_fct_man_0721_en-US.pdf), table 6-1, printed page 95. Section 6.3.1 describes modal cycle parameters.
- Heidenhain: an explicit chain with one `FUNCTION DWELL TIME` block. `crates/post/tests/heidenhain_cycles.rs`.
- The lathe posts and the posts with no canned cycle refuse the Back bore by name.

## Tests

Pins (`camcraft-motion`, lib):

- `drilling::tests_backbore::back_bore_carries_the_dwell`
- `drilling::tests_backbore::back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`

Post pins (`camcraft-post`):

- `sinumerik_g89_dwell_posts_p_in_milliseconds`
- `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p`

Red on unchanged code:

- `back_bore_carries_the_dwell`: `G89 dwells at the bottom: the cycle record carries the user's 1.5 s, got 0`.
- `back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`: `left: Some(500.0) right: Some(100.0)`.

Mutations:

- The old feed-out feed (`p.feed`) put back: `back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed` is red. Restored: green.
- `CycleKind::BackBore` removed from the dwell list: `back_bore_carries_the_dwell` is red. Restored: green.

Gate on final head `766540356cab0fc156ea47466977f9432e0eeae4`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS, 69 steps, 0 failed, 6.1 minutes. 1126 tests passed; 16 were ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS, no warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: PASS, 217 steps, 0 failed, 27.5 minutes. The three checks for known failures in #1950 failed as expected. The gate accepted those expected failures.
- Reached lanes: motion heavy and app heavy. Tested head: `766540356cab0fc156ea47466977f9432e0eeae4`.
- Motion heavy: 56 tests passed. Two known-failure checks for #1950 failed as expected and the gate accepted them.
- App heavy: 42 tests passed. One known-failure check for #1950 failed as expected and the gate accepted it.
- Sinumerik mutations: removing the milliseconds scale made `sinumerik_g89_dwell_posts_p_in_milliseconds` fail (`P1`, expected `P500`). Restoring the scale made it pass. Restoring the old P condition made `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p` fail (the second G89 had no `P0`). Restoring the fix made both tests pass.
- Commands used `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty. No recorded program has a Back bore that the generator makes.

## Not exercised

- No test posts a generated Back bore with a dwell from the operation to the G-code in one run. The generator pin and the post pins meet at the `Cycle` record.
- The Heidenhain post writes the Back bore as an explicit chain. Its retract line now has the plunge feed for a generated Back bore. The existing Heidenhain test uses a recorded chain and did not change.
- The UI was not started.

## Behaviour that changes for a program with no dwell

A Back bore with no dwell keeps the same F. The Sinumerik G89 block now includes `P0` to clear a previous dwell. Its `.cl` chain changes: the feed out is now the plunge feed. The simulation time of the retract changes with it.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes a file in `crates/motion/src/drilling/`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Back bore (G89) holes now carry the dwell at the bottom, and the toolpath feeds out at the plunge feed, as the canned cycle does. Sinumerik G89 clears the dwell when it changes to zero.

title: feat(fidelity): vouch for a mesh of unknown fidelity (VouchModelFidelity)
body:
## What changed

- A new undoable command, `VouchModelFidelity { model, by }`, clears the "fidelity unknown" mark of one model. It also clears the mark of each stock that is copied straight from that model.
- The command is one labelled undo step. The label names the person who vouched. Undo puts each mark back.
- The command refuses by name:
  - a model with a recorded coarse chord (#864);
  - an incomplete model (#1610);
  - a model that is not marked;
  - a name that is not a model;
  - an empty name of the person who vouches.
- A new component, `FidelityVouched { by, rev }`, records who vouched. The record is valid only while the model has the same geometry revision and no fidelity flag.
- The project file keeps the record in the optional key `fidelity_vouched` of the model row. There is no project version step.
- The MCP tool `vouch_model_fidelity { model, by }` runs the same command. `get_job` shows `models[].fidelity_vouched`. A script uses the tool through `cam.call`.
- The model page shows a name field and the button "Vouch for this mesh" below the "Fidelity unknown" line. A vouched model shows who vouched.

## Cause

Since project v59, each mesh of an older project without a recorded chord loads as "fidelity unknown" (#1056). The gate refuses its operations until a re-import. A model whose source file is gone, or whose mesh is exact, had no other path to a post.

title: feat(2d): place typed text as single-line engraving strokes (InsertText, MCP insert_text)
body:
First slice of #2679. This PR does not close the issue.

## What changed

- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/` is new. It holds our own single-line engraving font and the layout of a typed string.
  - `glyphs.rs` is the glyph table: capital letters, digits, the space and `- _ . : / # + = ( )`. Each glyph is straight strokes on a 4 x 6 grid.
  - `mod.rs` has `strokes()` (polylines in mm) and `sketch()` (a `SketchData` on the layer `text`).
- `crates/app/src/commands/insert_text.rs` is new. `InsertText` is an undoable command. It places the typed text as a `Sketch` on the top face of the stock of a setup, at X, Y and an angle.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/sketch_tools.rs` has the new MCP tool `insert_text`. It calls `InsertText`.
- `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` lists the tool.
- `docs/decisions/2679-engrave-typed-text.md` records the decisions.

The text profile is the same entity as a DXF profile. `move_dxf_profile`, `DeleteEntity`, `get_job` and the project file work on it with no change. The project file format does not change.

## Cause

There was no way to make 2D geometry from typed text. A user had to draw the letters in a CAD program and import a DXF file.

Two facts of `main` set the scope of this slice:

1. The issue says to use a font from `assets/ui/fonts/`. The repository holds no font file. The outlines of the `egui` default fonts need a font parser as a new dependency. A new dependency waits for the maintainer. This PR uses our own stroke font, drawn from scratch. A single-line stroke is also the correct input for the centreline Engrave generator: it gives a solid mark, not a hollow letter.
2. On `main`, an operation on a profile refuses generation by name ("a toolpath from the chains of a DXF profile is not generated yet"). #1869 adds Engrave and Trace on sketch chains, and #1869 depends on #1864 (PR #2716). The toolpath, the verify and the golden CL of #2679 need #1869.

## Refusals by name

- An empty text.
- A character with no glyph. A lower-case letter is refused. It is not changed to a capital, because a silent change puts a wrong mark on a part.
- A cap height outside 0.5 mm to 1000 mm. A letter spacing outside 0 mm to 1000 mm. More than 256 characters.
- A placement that is not finite or is more than 1e6 mm from the stock origin.
- A setup that does not exist. A setup with no stock. A name in use or a reserved name.
- `stroke_text::sketch` fails if a stroke does not chain clean. A text profile cannot hold a rejected chain.

## Tests

Pins (red before the change: the test files did not compile, `unresolved import camcraft_geometry::stroke_text`):

- `crates/geometry/tests/stroke_text.rs`

- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/mod.rs`: `the_character_set_is_the_glyph_table`, `each_glyph_stays_in_its_box`
- `crates/app/tests/insert_text.rs`

  - `a_text_profile_saves_and_loads_with_its_strokes_and_place`

title: feat(post): Sodick wire skim passes state their flushing

## What changed

- A wire machine file can state `edm.skim_flushing` (`high` or `low`). It is the flushing of each skim pass.
- `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` writes its T word (T84 / T85) before each skim's C word.
- The header of the program names the skim flushing word.
- `edm.skim_flushing` needs `edm.flushing`. The machine file parser, `Edm::is_sane`, `Edm::refusal` and the post refuse a file that states only the skim flushing.
- A skim on a machine that states `edm.flushing` and no `edm.skim_flushing` is refused by name. The app writes no file.
- A machine that states no flushing posts its skims as before (#2649).
- The post's machine mirror carries the key only when it is stated.
- The machine editor has a "Skim flushing" choice. It is enabled only while a flushing is stated.
- The MCP `edit_machine` tool takes the key through the same undoable machine patch. No new command is added.
- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` writes a note that a stated skim flushing is not programmed.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/2686-sodick-skim-flushing.md`.

## Cause

Since #2649, the Sodick post writes each skim on its own C word. It wrote the flushing word after the threading only. A skim ran on the rough cut's flushing, and the program did not say so. The project had no value for the flushing of a skim.

title: fix(2d): drop near-zero loops from the pocket region on a part
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs` (`minus_standing`): the result "enclosed area minus standing part material" loses each loop whose absolute area is below `ISLAND_AREA_MIN` (1e-4 mm2).
- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/slivers.rs`: new method `Region::without_slivers(min_area)`. It filters loops. It does not change a kept loop. A measure that is not positive and finite removes nothing.
- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs`: one line, `mod slivers;`.
- `crates/geometry/tests/region_slivers.rs`: two new tests for the method.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/frame_cost_probe.rs`: new pin `area_preview_of_the_default_containment_is_filled`. The helper `adaptive_preview` keeps its behaviour and calls the new `adaptive_preview_with(h, patch, containment)`. The pin selects the welded face with the most strips itself (the concave outer wall of fig8).
- `docs/decisions/2766-preview-sliver-loops.md`: the decision entry.

## Cause

The pocket family on a part cuts the enclosed area minus the part material that stands in it. The enclosed area and the part section share a wall. The two tessellations of that wall disagree by about 1 um. The difference then has 3-point loops of 5e-9 to 1.5e-7 mm2. A clockwise loop of that kind stands outside each boundary. `Region::triangles` refuses the whole region with "hole outside any boundary". Thus `boundary_viz::preview_fill` gave `None` for the biggest fig8 patch with the default Containment.

`selection_region` gives the same region to generation. Thus the slivers also reached generation. This fix removes them there too.

## Screenshots

Both captures use the same fig8 concave outer-wall patch with default Containment and the Boundary group open.
The before capture disables the sliver filter in `minus_standing` to reproduce the missing fill.
The after capture uses the restored PR head.

body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate light` is a new gate tier. It runs the light twins of the heavy tests in release.
- The plan is one release build of the crates that hold a twin. Then it has one step for each test target with a twin (`motion light: lib`).
- A light twin is found from the source. Its ignore reason starts with `light lane:`. Its name is `<full test>_light`.
- The planner refuses a twin by name when its file has no `#[ignore]`d full test. A twin cannot take the place of its full test.
- The first twin is `the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/tests.rs`. It plans the slot 2 times. The full sweep keeps its 20 rows and does not change.
- A red light run prints a note for the PR. The note names each red step and the command of its full heavy step: `cargo xtask gate release --only "motion heavy: lib"`.
- AGENTS.md has two new named rules: **The light lane** ("Testing") and **Local full rerun** ("Commits and Releases").
- `docs/decisions/2569-light-heavy-tier.md` records the choices.
- The branch was refreshed against `upstream/main` at `744c0847b`. The merge keeps the upstream `heavy` tier and the new `light` tier.
- The tier pins now check both parser variants, both help lines, both error lists, and both rules in AGENTS.md.

## Cause

body:
# Current head `1e6cd8ec2` (2026-11-19 rework)

This head answers the review of 2026-11-19 (all three points). The branch now carries the updated parent #2663 head (`ae4f36fca`) and current `origin/main` (`744c0847b`). GitHub shows MERGEABLE. #2663 must still merge first; this PR then takes a refresh at merge time if needed.

## Stacked on #2663

This branch is cut from #2663's branch, because both change the tool pages. The base is `main`, so the file list also shows #2663's files. The delta for this PR is: commit `963d7c38`, commit `1fea5669`, and the two new commits `423c3551c` and `1e6cd8ec2` on top of the merge `d7f8a85cf`.

## What changed

The tool body and profile editor gets its own window. Properties now holds only the tool's settings.

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs` - new `tool_shape_editor_window` (`Tool shape: <name>`, 620x640, scrolling body, fixed `Close`). The old combined `tool_editor_window` is gone.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings.rs` - Properties shows the settings grid, one side preview, `Delete`, `Apply` / `Add tool`, and the `Edit tool shape` door.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs` and `tool_cutter_page.rs` - two columns inside the window: controls left, points and side view right. The holder library comes first, then the Body / Profile tabs.
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`, `actions.rs` - `State::tool_shape_editor`, `State::new_tool_form`, `open_tool_shape_editor`, `begin_new_tool`, `close_tool_shape_editor`.
- `docs/decisions/2397-tool-shape-window.md` - the decision record.

## Review point 1: `Edit tool shape` was unreachable after `Add tool`

Fixed in code by `423c3551c`. When `Add tool` lands, the page now targets the saved tool in the same frame. The page leaves the `New tool` form and shows the saved tool's normal controls, including `Edit tool shape`. No second tool-browser click is needed.

| ![before add tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr2764-before-add-tool.png) | ![after add tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr2764-after-add-tool.png) |

The left image shows the stuck form: the tool landed, but the page kept the `New tool` draft. The right image shows the saved tool `Tool2`: heading, `Delete`, and the `Edit tool shape` door.

## Review point 2: the waterjet recipe feed widget

Fixed by the merge `d7f8a85cf`, which carries the parent #2663 head `ae4f36fca`. That head gives the recipe Feed row the `num_feed_row` feed widget. The pin `waterjet_recipe_feed_row_reads_as_a_feed_rate_in_both_unit_modes` passes on this head.

The merge needed one repair commit (`1e6cd8ec2`): both sides had rewritten `tests/waterjet_recipe.rs` for different layouts, and the auto-merge mixed them. The harness clicked a header the grid removed, and one pin queried the old tool window. The pins now target the Properties page again. All four waterjet pins pass.

## Review point 3: before and after screenshots

The images come from the headless pixel-snapshot harness (1600x1500, seeded document, `EM-0600-4FL`). They sit on the images-only branch `pr-screenshots` of my fork. No snapshot PNG enters this PR's branch.

Shape editor: `main` carries the shape inside the combined `Tool: <name>` window. This head puts it in its own `Tool shape: <name>` window, opened by `Edit tool shape`.

## Pinning tests

- new: `egui_app::tests::tool_shape_window::add_tool_selects_the_saved_tool_and_opens_its_shape` - drives View, Tool library..., New tool..., Add tool, then Edit tool shape, with no browser selection after the add.

- `tool_editor_structure`, `tool_cutter_params_structure`

No test was deleted or ignored. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Gate on the final head `1e6cd8ec2`

- `cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --test-threads=6`: 1254 passed, 4 failed, 7 ignored (136 s).
- The 4 failures are only the `frame_cost_probe` / `frame_cost_caches` probes at `frame_cost_probe.rs:278` ("the area preview is filled"). Previously, `sketch_model::generation_problem` refused all operations on DXF profiles. Also, `FeatureSel` had no sketch keys, and ray picking skipped sketch geometry.

title: feat(2d): Slot Undercut for T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop cutters
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the Slot Undercut operation and the cutters for it.

- **Four cutter kinds** in `camcraft-tools`: `t_slot`, `keyseat`, `dovetail`, `lollipop`. They use the existing tool fields. `diameter` is the head. `flute_len` is the head height. `shank_d` and `shank_len` are the neck. `tip_angle` is the dovetail flank angle. The kind words are additive, so `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. The starter catalog has one cutter of each kind.
- **One generator** in `camcraft-motion` (`machining2d::undercut`). It cuts a straight slot or a circular slot (DXF-style bulge). It changes Z at one XY station only, outside the wall. It feeds in sideways, cuts the centre pass and the radial stepover passes at one depth, feeds out the same way, then lifts. The pass offset comes from the widest point of the cutter profile, not from the tip.
- **One verify law** in `camcraft-sim` (`Mode::Undercut`, `verify/undercut.rs`). A move that changes Z while material is in or over the head is `Warning::UndercutLift`. It blocks the post. A neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a `ShankHit`. The operation layer reads the two again against the stock that the earlier operations left (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`). A neck slot that an earlier Slot operation cut is then air.
- **The true profile in the solid law.** The solid law judges a dovetail as a frustum and a lollipop as a full ball (`Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`). The head top gets the same allowance as the tip, so a head that stands under its roof is contact and not a gouge.
- **The true profile in the field stock simulation** (`Stock::simulate_undercut`, `Stock::with_partial_undercut`, `SdfTool::Dovetail`). The head and the neck are two convex solids. The field keeps their union. Both the stock view and Simulate playback cut the head and neck with it. Notice `cut_twin_work::twin_tool` maps `SdfTool::Dovetail` to `"dovetail"`.
- **The column engines cut nothing for an undercut.** A column has one top for each (x, y). It cannot hold air below material.
- **App**: `OpParams::SlotUndercut` (kind tag 44, appended), the project file mirror (keeping `0.0` `bulge` and `neck_slot` keys in JSON), the stamp digest, heights, the part solid law for a part source, and the kept-parts law for both stock and part sources.
- **MCP**: `add_operation` with kind `Slot Undercut` (key `slot_undercut`) and `add_tool` with the new kind words. `verify` reports the new finding kind `undercut_lift`. `list_operation_types` and `edit_operation` include `bulge` and `neck_slot` when they equal `0.0`.
- **UI**: the four undercut kinds in the tool editor (`tool_undercut_row.rs` seeds valid defaults, `Flank angle (deg)` / `flank angle °` edits `ToolKind::Dovetail`, and `Corner radius` stays hidden for undercut kinds), the Slot Undercut page (`undercut_page.rs`), and five original icons (SVG masters rendered with `cargo xtask icons`).
- **Docs**: a Slot Undercut section in the 2D operations guide, and `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md`.

## UI screenshots

Before/after renders from the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU) on `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`) and this PR branch (images stored on `mkinney/Camcraft` `pr-screenshots` commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`):

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

There was no cutter kind with a head wider than its neck, and no operation for one. The laws for a plain contour are wrong below a roof. The column model reads a pass as a cleared kerf, so a lift through the roof passes as a retract in its own kerf.

## Tests

New pins cover the new behaviour. Each review fix below also has a direct test and mutation check.

- `camcraft-tools --lib` (`107 passed; 0 failed`): `undercut::tests` checks sane cutters, refusals by name, the profile contact point, and the drawn outline.
- `camcraft-motion --lib` (`459 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`): `machining2d::undercut::tests` pins single-station Z moves, entry slot refusals, concentric arc slots, profile contact offsets, and input refusals.
- `camcraft-sim --test undercut_laws` (`14 passed; 0 failed`): pins `UndercutLift`, `ShankHit`, `acquit_undercut_by_prior`, `Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`, `Atom::cap`, and `Stock::simulate_undercut`.
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_slot_undercut` (`7 passed; 0 failed`): pins MCP cutting, verification, posting, refusals, `a_part_source_undercut_keeps_neighbouring_parts`, and `list_operation_types_and_edit_operation_keep_zero_bulge_and_neck_slot`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play` (`8 passed; 0 failed`): pins `playback_removes_undercut_head_and_neck_and_matches_field_view`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play_partial` (`4 passed; 0 failed`): pins `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy`.
- `camcraft-motion --test golden_undercut`: pins four golden CL files. The generator suite and its unchanged goldens now live in `crates/motion/tests/`.
- `camcraft-app --test tool_law` (`5 passed; 0 failed`): pins undercut cutter compatibility.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` (`1256 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`): includes `tool_undercut_row::tests`, `tool_cutter_params::each_milling_kind_shows_the_parameters_its_outline_is_drawn_from`, and `tests/tool_undercut.rs` (`new_tool_undercut_kinds_seed_sane_defaults_hide_corner_radius_and_show_dovetail_flank_angle`, `dovetail_properties_and_editor_edit_flank_angle_without_corner_radius`, and `slot_undercut_page_shows_its_geometry_heights_passes_and_feeds_fields`).

Review-fix mutation checks (guard reverted -> RED, restored -> GREEN):

- UI dovetail flank angle, undercut defaults, and corner-radius filter reverted: RED (`3 failed` across `tests/tool_undercut.rs` and `tool_cutter_params`). Restored: GREEN (`11 passed; 0 failed`).
- `is_part_kept_kind` reverted in `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`: `a_part_source_undercut_keeps_neighbouring_parts` RED (`post` succeeded instead of refusing). Restored: GREEN (`7 passed; 0 failed`).
- `skip_serializing_if = "is_zero"` restored in `crates/app/src/project/undercut_dto.rs`: `list_operation_types_and_edit_operation_keep_zero_bulge_and_neck_slot` RED (`list_operation_types` omitted `bulge` and `neck_slot`). Restored: GREEN (`7 passed; 0 failed`).
- `stock_play.rs` and `stock_play_head.rs` undercut playback handling reverted: `playback_removes_undercut_head_and_neck_and_matches_field_view` and `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy` RED. Restoring `stock_play.rs` alone kept `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy` RED. Restored both: GREEN (`8 passed; 0 failed` and `4 passed; 0 failed`).

Gate on `b95c27b2e52fc8b976ce9372bcc5e4141c247113`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 651 steps with zero failures (45.9 minutes). The merged main revision is `e5b0ca3c1`. It includes #2767, which fixes the four reviewed area-preview failures. The UI unit suite passed 1,258 tests (7 ignored). All 16 UI integration suites passed. `cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed with zero warnings.

Latest review-fix checks:

- The motion `golden_undercut` suite passed all four tests. Removing the motion test target gave RED. A feed change from 120 to 121 made all four goldens fail. Restoring the suite and feed returned all four tests to GREEN. The four CL files moved without byte changes.
- Reverting the main geometry fix gave exactly the four reviewed frame-cost failures. Restoring it returned all eight frame-cost tests to GREEN.
- The temporary literature audit gave RED on the old decision (0/8 checks) and GREEN on the updated decision (8/8). The decision records checked sources, design choices, and limitations. No audit script or review evidence is on this branch.

Current merge blocker: main advanced to `744c0847b04d54cfc6e3e8b24a21520c40b6bcef` during validation. A later local refresh exposes safety overlaps: `verify/avoid_poly.rs:25` omits `Atom::cap`, and `verify/swept.rs:130` omits `Prof::Dove` and `Prof::Ball` in keep-out dilation. The refresh compile checks and clippy are RED. The gate was stopped after the compile failures. No new collision semantics were selected. Local commit `b8c5cb42e` is not pushed. The pushed head and its GREEN gate remain `b95c27b2e`. The `Addressed:` comment records the blocker.

## Goldens moved

No existing golden changed. Four golden CL files are new:

- `slot_undercut_tslot_straight.cl`
- `slot_undercut_keyseat_arc.cl`
- `slot_undercut_dovetail_straight.cl`
- `slot_undercut_lollipop_arc.cl`

No snapshot PNG changed. Five icon PNGs are new (`cargo xtask icons` wrote them from the new SVG masters and changed no other PNG).

## Not exercised

- The literature search ran during the latest review fix. `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md` records checked handbook, Autodesk behaviour, and research sources for entry, exit, profiles, and field simulation. It records the limits of those sources and the implementation. The search used the web tool because Perplexity was unavailable. The implementation preceded this search.
- Dovetail and lollipop parts are not tested through the app. Their profiles are tested in the sim crate (solid law and field stock) and the generator.
- The program verdict before a post reads the stock from above. It does not show the undercut as removed. The undercut law and the solid law judge the operation instead.
- A flipped WCS and a rotated work offset refuse the kind. An aligned setup and a WCS yaw do not list it. No 3+2 tilt.
- One depth level for each operation. The far end of a blind slot stays square. The centre line is typed, not picked.
- Issue #896 (form cutters with a drawn outline, corner rounding, slitting saw) stays open. This PR adds only the four parametric kinds that #1444 needs.

## Overlaps

No open PR changes the same function. These open PRs change other functions in the same files. The PR that merges second refreshes.

- #2678, #2149: `mcp/job.rs`, `operation/generate.rs`, `project/file.rs`, `verify/mod.rs`, `verify/probe.rs`, `verify/types.rs`, `ui/state.rs`
- #2675, #2666: `operation/generate.rs`

- #2665, #2662, #1798: `ui/state.rs` (#1798 also `icons.rs`)

#2670, #2563, #1713, #1798, #2665, #2712, #2715, #2730, #2731, #2741, and #2742 merged while this work ran. Their changes are in the branch through the merge of `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`).

title: fix(fidelity)!: a stock copy of an incomplete model keeps naming its hole
body:
A stock copied from an incomplete model (#1610) now keeps naming that model's hole after the model is deleted. Before this change, its refusal at the post fell back to "saved before CamCraft recorded mesh fidelity (project v58 or older)". The post still refused it; only the reason given was wrong.


## What changed

The copy's refusal read the hole from the source model by name (`mesh_open::unknown_note`), so once the source was gone the lookup found nothing. Now the copy carries the hole itself (`schema::MeshOpen`), beside the fidelity-unknown sentinel it already carried (#1056):

- **Where the hole is copied:** every place that lands the sentinel on a copy now lands the hole with it:
  - `SetStock` and its undo
  - a setup clone (`CreateSetup` with a datum)
  - an undone `DeleteSetup`
  - `UpdateModel`'s refresh of the copies, and its undo
  - the project loader
- **Where the refusal reads it:** `model_fidelity::op_problem` reads the hole off the entity that carries the sentinel. Two small helpers: `mesh_open::hole_behind` (the twin of `model_fidelity::chord_behind`) and `mesh_open::note_for`.
- **Project file:** the saver already wrote `mesh_open` for any entity that has one. The loader now also accepts it on a `FromModel` stock marked `fidelity_unknown`, and a hole without the mark stays corrupt. This is an incompatible project-file change: #1610's check (commit `35b3422cf`) shipped in v0.21.0 through v0.24.0, and those readers refuse `mesh_open` on any entity that is not a model marked `fidelity_unknown` as corrupt, so a project file written with a hole on a `FromModel` stock row does not open in v0.21.0 to v0.24.0 (main now writes project version 71, which those releases also reject as unsupported). The commit carries `fix(fidelity)!:` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer; see `docs/decisions/1700-stock-copy-hole.md`.

The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/1700-stock-copy-hole.md`.

## How tested

- **New:** `crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs` (7 tests). A copy carries the hole, and its refusal names the source and the hole:
  - after the source is deleted, and across undo and redo of that delete;
  - after save, load, and a second save that matches byte for byte;
  - through a setup clone and an undone setup delete;
  - through a whole re-import of the source (which clears it) and that re-import's undo;
  - through `SetStock`'s undo.

  The file also checks that a stock with a hole and no mark fails to load as corrupt.
- **Without the fix,** the two "source deleted" tests fail: the refusal reads "saved before CamCraft recorded …".
- **Existing tests:** the `import_step_open_shell` tests from #1610 still pass. Its corrupt-file message check passes too, because the new message keeps the old wording as a prefix.
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (112 app suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branched from upstream/main after #1699 merged, not from a cut tag: the code this fixes is not in v0.20.0.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Changelog: Stock copies of incomplete models now keep naming their source model's hole after the source is deleted, and keep naming the hole for projects saved in v0.21.0 to v0.24.0. Breaking: such project files do not open in v0.21.0 to v0.24.0.

Fixes #1700
